advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Measure the list budget against the actual serialized wire shape (post model_validate / js_safe_result) or add margin, since raw-dict measurement under-counts stringified ns timestamps.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_budget.py:93: `size = _payload_bytes({"result": rows})` measures the pre-validation raw rows
list_tickets wraps the bounded rows in TicketStateOut.model_validate AFTER the bound (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:333-336)
js_safe_result stringifies out-of-range ints, increasing byte length: src/rebar/_errors path js_safe_result at _mcp_errors.py:187-190 `return str(value)`
docstring claims the workflow budget is 'airtight regardless of shape' and the list bound reuses the same budget
advisory.finding: The list budget is measured on raw dict rows (json.dumps({'result': rows}, default=str)) but the actual serialized wire payload passes through TicketStateOut.model_validate and js_safe_result, which converts JS-unsafe 19-digit nanosecond integers into longer decimal strings; the measured size can be smaller than the true wire size, so the 'airtight' bound may still let an over-budget payload onto the wire.
scenarios: A list whose raw size sits just under 90_000 bytes but crosses the budget once ns timestamps are stringified and models re-serialized

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving TicketView.list_by_query with a parent-bounded include_body=False query against signature-carrying child states, asserting authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring are dropped (and present under include_body=True).
evidence: src/rebar/_snapshot/ticket_view.py:388: `item = lean_projection(item)` is an ADDED line changing the snapshot lean shape from a 2-field pop to a 6-field projection.

reads.py docstring for lean_projection: 'shared by the event-log read path (list_states) and the snapshot read path (rebar._snapshot.ticket_view.TicketView.list_by_query) so the two backends cannot drift'.
tests/unit/test_ticket_query.py:100-104 asserts only `"description" not in lean[0] and "comments" not in lean[0]` on reads.list_states — never the snapshot backend and never the new signature fields.

tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py:346-347 calls list_by_query but asserts only ticket_id, not the lean projection; TicketQuery.include_body defaults True so the lean branch is not exercised there.
ABSENCE: search for `include_body=False` in tests yields only test_ticket_query.py:101 (event-log path); no snapshot-backend lean test exists.

Named violating input: `list_by_query(TicketQuery(parent=<parent_id>, include_body=False))` against a child state carrying `authorship_ledger`/`attestations`/`signature`/`keyring` — the added line would be the only thing dropping them, and a regression reverting it to the old 2-field pop would go undetected.
advisory.finding: The snapshot read backend's lean projection change (TicketView.list_by_query now calls lean_projection, dropping authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring in addition to description/comments) has no test. The 'cannot drift between backends' parity contract is asserted by the module docstring but only verified on the event-log path (list_states, via the facade test); no test drives list_by_query(TicketQuery(parent=..., include_body=False)) against signature-carrying states to prove the snapshot backend actually omits the four signature fields.
scenarios: A completion read through the pinned snapshot view requests a lean parent-bounded list; the snapshot backend silently reverts to leaking signature bulk if lean_projection is refactored out of that path.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the ready_tickets wire-shape change (lean-by-default, signature+body fields dropped) is an intended, documented backward-incompatible change for MCP clients.
evidence: src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:377: def ready_tickets(sort: str | None = None, full: bool = False) -> list[TicketStateOut]:
ready_states returns public_state rows with signature material intact: src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:552 `states = [public_state(s) for s in find_ready_tickets(...)]`
Prior body returned bodies unprojected: diff shows old `return [TicketStateOut.model_validate(t) for t in rebar.ready(sort=sort)]` with no projection
blocking.finding: ready_tickets is now lean-by-default: it previously returned the full ticket shape (bodies plus authorship_ledger/attestations/signature/keyring, since ready_states -> public_state retains those and there was no include_body flag), and now drops all of them unless full=True. This is a wire-shape/behavior change for existing MCP clients that consumed those fields from ready_tickets.
scenarios: An MCP client that read description/comments/signature off a ready_tickets row now gets them stripped by default

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the `ready_tickets` MCP tool default-output narrowing (full shape -> lean by default, dropping `description`/`comments`) is an intended, documented behavior change and not a silent break for existing clients.
evidence: OLD (diff): `return [TicketStateOut.model_validate(t) for t in rebar.ready(sort=sort)]` — no projection, full shape

NEW: `def ready_tickets(sort: str | None = None, full: bool = False)` then `_discovery_rows(rebar.ready(sort=sort), full=full, bound=_bound_list_payload, tool="ready_tickets")` which does `[lean_projection(row) for row in rows]` when not full (_mcp_reads.py:392)
`description`/`comments` are DECLARED schema fields with defaults on TicketStateOut (_mcp_models.py:114-115), so the schema stays valid but the default CONTENT changes

ABSENCE: grep of `rebar.ready(` consumers (tests/interfaces/queries/test_ready_output.py, test_session_log_visibility.py, etc.) shows callers read only `ticket_id`; no in-repo consumer reads `description`/`comments` off a ready() result, so no in-repo callsite breaks — the exposure is to external MCP clients
blocking.finding: The MCP `ready_tickets` tool's DEFAULT output shape narrowed: pre-change it returned the full ticket shape (unprojected `rebar.ready(sort=sort)`, including `description` and `comments`); post-change the new `full: bool = False` default runs `lean_projection`, so by default `description`/`comments` (and the signature fields) are no longer emitted. This is an unversioned change to the default emitted content of a public MCP read tool — an existing client that read `description`/`comments` off `ready_tickets` now receives the schema default (null/empty) unless it starts passing `full=True`.
scenarios: An external MCP client that called `ready_tickets` and read each row's `description`/`comments` now silently gets null/empty by default

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 287 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug 494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan 494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review 494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan 494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
